items.en: We'll put a hold of $450 on your card, which drops to $150 if you take the full coverage.
items.ja: カードに450ドルの仮押さえをします。フル補償に入れば150ドルになります。
items.speaker: hamlet
items.note: drops to の後が補償ありの額。差額300は罠
items.tts: We'll put a hold of four-fifty on your card, which drops to one-fifty if you take the full coverage.
items.ask: フル補償なら いくら押さえる？

items.en: If you can sign by Friday, I might be able to get my manager to sweeten the deal a little.
items.ja: 金曜までにご契約いただければ、上司に掛け合って条件を少し良くできるかもしれません。 → つまり、早く決めれば値引きの可能性がある。
items.speaker: maple
choices: A better offer may be possible if you decide soon.
Her manager has already approved a discount.
The offer ends on Friday whatever happens.
items.note: might be able to は未確定。sweeten＝条件を良くする

items.en: So, can we shake on twelve percent, or do you need to run it by your team first?
items.ja: では12パーセントで手を打ちますか、それともまずチームに確認が必要ですか？ →「確認は要りますが、前向きです。」
items.speaker: octavian
choices: I'd need to check with them, but I'm optimistic.
Yes, I run with my team every week.
We shook on it last year, actually.
items.note: run it by＝確認を取る。shake on＝合意する
items.tts: So, can we shake on twelve percent, or d'you need to run it by your team first?

items.en: This is the third time I've called about this, and every time I'm told someone'll call me back.
items.ja: この件で電話するのは3回目で、毎回折り返すと言われるんです。 →「申し訳ありません。解決するまで私が担当します。」
items.speaker: pekoe
choices: I'm so sorry. I'll stay on this with you until it's resolved.
Of course, someone will call you back.
That's right, it's your third time.
items.note: 「また折り返します」は火に油。担当を約束するのが正解

items.en: I appreciate you're only following policy, but I'd like to speak to someone who can actually make a decision.
items.ja: あなたが規則に従っているだけなのはわかりますが、実際に判断できる方と話したいです。 → つまり、上の人を出してほしい。
items.speaker: olivia
choices: She wants to talk to a manager.
She agrees with the policy.
She'll make the decision herself.
items.note: someone who can make a decision＝上司を出して

items.en: Right. So I ordered a king-size, and what's turned up is, generously, a large single.
items.ja: で、キングサイズを頼んだのに、届いたのは、甘く見ても大きめのシングルだ。 → つまり、ずっと小さいものが届いた。
items.speaker: chief
choices: He got a much smaller bed than he ordered.
He got a bigger bed than he ordered.
He's happy with what arrived.
items.note: generously＝甘く見ても。届いたのは大幅に小さい

items.en: I was quoted $79 a month, but I've been charged $97 for three months now.
items.ja: 月79ドルと言われたのに、もう3か月も97ドル請求されているんです。
items.speaker: molly
items.note: 79と97の逆転に注意。差額18×3か月
items.tts: I was quoted seventy-nine a month, but I've been charged ninety-seven for three months now.
items.ask: 払いすぎた 合計は？

items.en: Excuse me, sorry to be a pain, but this is barely warm in the middle.
items.ja: すみません、面倒をかけて申し訳ないんですが、これ真ん中がほとんど温かくないです。 →「失礼しました。すぐ作り直させます。」
items.speaker: anchovy
choices: Oh, I'm so sorry. I'll have the kitchen redo it.
No pain, no gain!
Sure, the middle table is free.
items.note: sorry to be a pain は前置き。本題は「ぬるい」

items.en: It was supposed to be here by Tuesday. It's now Friday.
items.ja: 火曜までに届くはずだったんです。今日はもう金曜ですよ。
items.speaker: francine
choices: supposed to
going to
due to
items.note: supposed to は s'posta と縮む。d はほぼ聞こえない
items.tts: It was s'posta be here by Tuesday. It's now Friday.

items.en: Don't get me wrong, I love a little music. I'd just love it a lot more before midnight.
items.ja: 誤解しないで、音楽は好きなんだ。ただ、夜中の12時前ならもっと好きなんだけどね。 → つまり、深夜の音楽をやめてほしい。
items.speaker: kabuki
choices: Please stop playing music so late.
He'd like to join in with the music.
Please play it louder before midnight.
items.note: ユーモアで包んだ騒音の苦情

items.en: Just to play devil's advocate, are we sure customers actually want this, or do we just want to build it?
items.ja: あえて反対の立場で言うけど、お客さんは本当にこれを求めてる？それとも僕らが作りたいだけ？ → つまり、計画に疑問がある。
items.speaker: bob
choices: He doubts customers really need it.
He fully supports building it.
He knows customers asked for it.
items.note: devil's advocate＝あえて反対意見を言う役

items.en: I see where you're coming from, but I'm not sure the numbers back that up.
items.ja: おっしゃることはわかりますが、数字がそれを裏付けているかは疑問です。 →「確かに。データを出して一緒に見ましょう。」
items.speaker: tammy
choices: Fair. Let me pull the data and we can look at it together.
I'm coming from the Chicago office.
Yes, I backed it all up last night.
items.note: see where you’re coming from は反論の前置き

items.en: With all due respect, that's not what was agreed in the last meeting.
items.ja: お言葉ですが、それは前回の会議で合意した内容と違います。 → つまり、強く反対している。
items.speaker: fang
choices: He firmly disagrees with what's being said.
He respects the decision and agrees.
He missed the last meeting.
items.note: With all due respect の後は強い反論

items.en: Honestly, I couldn't agree more, but that's not the part I'm worried about.
items.ja: 正直、大賛成よ。でも私が心配しているのはそこじゃないの。
items.speaker: nana
choices: couldn't
could
wouldn't
items.note: couldn't agree more＝大賛成。could との差は n't

items.en: Can we park that for now and come back to it once we've seen the budget?
items.ja: それはいったん置いておいて、予算を見てから戻りませんか？ →「いいですね。来週の議題に入れましょう。」
items.speaker: reneigh
choices: Sure, let's put it on next week's agenda.
The parking lot's full, I'm afraid.
I've already seen it, thanks.
items.note: park＝いったん保留する。駐車の話ではない

items.en: Purple for a law firm's logo? Well, it'll certainly get noticed.
items.ja: 法律事務所のロゴに紫？ まあ、確かに目立つでしょうね。 → つまり、いいとは思っていない。
items.speaker: katt
choices: She doesn't think it works.
She thinks it's eye-catching and perfect.
She wants it to stand out even more.
items.note: certainly get noticed は婉曲な否定。褒めていない

items.en: I think we're going around in circles. Can we just agree to disagree and move on?
items.ja: 堂々巡りになってる気がする。意見の違いは違いとして、先に進めない？ →「いいよ。両方の意見を議事録に残そう。」
items.speaker: beau
choices: Fine by me. Let's note both views in the minutes.
Sure, I agree with you completely.
The circle chart is on slide three.
items.note: agree to disagree＝違いを認めて先へ。賛成ではない

items.en: As you know, we've been reviewing the team structure, and unfortunately, your role is one of the ones affected.
items.ja: ご存じのとおりチーム体制を見直してきたが、残念ながら君の職もその対象になった。 → つまり、ポジションがなくなる。
items.speaker: tom-nook
choices: Your job is being cut.
You're being promoted to a new role.
The review will happen next year.
items.note: role is affected は「職がなくなる」の婉曲表現

items.en: Unfortunately, the board decided not to go ahead with the project, at least for this year.
items.ja: 残念ながら、役員会は少なくとも今年はこのプロジェクトを進めないと決めました。 →「残念です。来年また動く可能性は？」
items.speaker: poppy
choices: That's disappointing. Any chance it comes back next year?
Great, so when do we start?
Go ahead, I'll wait.
items.note: not go ahead＝中止。at least で来年に余地

items.en: The parts are on back order, so we're looking at six to eight weeks, not the two we said.
items.ja: 部品が入荷待ちなので、お伝えした2週間ではなく、6〜8週間かかりそうです。
items.speaker: lucky
choices: 8週間
2週間
6週間
items.note: not the two we said は前の約束。最長は8
items.tts: The parts are on back order, so we're lookin' at six to eight weeks, not the two we said.
items.ask: 新しい見込みは 最長 何週間？

items.en: Thanks so much for your time. The team really enjoyed meeting you, but we decided to go in a different direction.
items.ja: お時間をありがとうございました。チームもお会いできて喜んでいましたが、別の方向で進めることになりました。 → つまり、不採用。
items.speaker: audie
choices: You didn't get the job.
They'd like a second interview.
The team is moving to a new office.
items.note: different direction＝不採用を伝える定型句

items.en: I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but your car's not going to be ready till Monday.
items.ja: 悪い知らせで申し訳ないけど、車は月曜まで仕上がらないんです。 →「うわ。それまで代車はありますか？」
items.speaker: teddy
choices: Ugh. Is there a loaner I could use till then?
Thanks, I'll bear that in mind.
Great, I'll pick it up today.
items.note: bearer of bad news＝悪い知らせを伝える役
items.tts: I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but your car's not gonna be ready till Monday.

items.en: I'm sorry, but we won't be able to fit you in until next month.
items.ja: 申し訳ありませんが、来月までご予約をお取りできません。
items.speaker: henry
choices: won't
will
wouldn't
items.note: won't は want と別の母音。否定を聞き逃さない

items.en: Starting in April, rent goes up from ¥142,000 to ¥149,500 a month.
items.ja: 4月から、家賃は月14万2千円から14万9千5百円に上がります。
items.speaker: curt
items.note: from→to の to の後が新しい家賃
items.tts: Starting in April, rent goes up from a hundred and forty-two thousand to a hundred and forty-nine thousand five hundred a month.
marks: a hundred and forty-nine thousand five hundred

items.en: Let's hit pause on pricing till legal's taken a look. No point locking anything in before then.
items.ja: 価格は法務が見るまでいったん止めよう。それまでに何かを確定しても意味がないから。 → つまり、価格は法務の確認待ち。
items.speaker: lily
choices: Pricing waits until legal has checked it.
Pricing has already been decided.
Legal will set the price.
items.note: hit pause＝一時停止。lock in＝確定する

items.en: So who's owning the follow-up with the vendor?
items.ja: で、業者とのフォローアップは誰が担当する？ →「私がやります。今日メールします。」
items.speaker: label
choices: I can take that. I'll email them today.
The vendor owns the building.
We followed the vendor on social media.
items.note: owning＝担当する。所有の意味ではない

items.en: Before we wrap up, are we all on the same page about the launch date?
items.ja: 終わる前に、発売日について全員認識は合ってる？
items.speaker: daisy-mae
choices: launch
lunch
last
items.note: launch と lunch は母音が違う。会議なら発売日

items.en: Let's table this until Thursday, when the whole team's there.
items.ja: この件は、全員がそろう木曜まで保留にしましょう。 → つまり、木曜まで先送りしたい。
items.speaker: wolfgang
choices: He wants to put it off until Thursday.
He wants to drop the topic for good.
He wants to decide it right now.
items.note: 米国の table は「保留・後回し」。議題に出すではない

items.en: Wow. Ninety minutes, and it could've been one email.
items.ja: うわ。90分もかけて、メール1通で済んだのに。
items.speaker: kk-slider
choices: could've
should've
would've
items.note: 皮肉。coulda＝could have。should との差は頭の音
items.tts: Wow. Ninety minutes, and it coulda been one email.

items.en: We're at 38 sign-ups, minus the 5 who canceled, plus the 3 from the Denver office.
items.ja: 申込みは38人、キャンセルの5人を引いて、デンバー支社の3人を足して。
items.speaker: stitches
items.note: 38−5＋3＝36。最初の数字は罠
items.tts: We're at thirty-eight sign-ups, minus the five who canceled, plus the three from the Denver office.

items.en: Noted. I'm not sure that'll fly with the client, but let's see what they say.
items.ja: 了解。それがクライアントに通るかは怪しいけど、反応を見てみよう。 → つまり、受け入れられないと思っている。
items.speaker: sterling
choices: He doubts the client will accept it.
He's sure the client will love it.
He'll fly out to meet the client.
items.note: fly＝通用する。飛行機の話ではない

items.en: Once we get the form, it's 3 to 5 business days for review, then another 10 for the card to arrive.
items.ja: 書類が届いてから審査に3〜5営業日、さらにカード到着まで10営業日です。
items.speaker: flick
items.tts: Once we get the form, it's three to five business days for review, then another ten for the card to arrive.

items.en: So you scan it, tag it, and then it goes to finance for sign-off. Does that make sense?
items.ja: スキャンしてタグを付けたら、経理の承認に回る。わかった？ →「だいたい。経理で止まったら誰に催促すれば？」
items.speaker: cj
choices: Mostly. Who do I bug if finance sits on it?
Yes, it makes sense to sign off now.
No, I've never been to finance.
items.note: Does that make sense? は確認。質問で返してよい

items.en: You can skip step four, technically. I just wouldn't, unless you enjoy starting again from scratch.
items.ja: 手順4は一応飛ばせるよ。私ならやらないけどね、一からやり直すのが好きなら別だけど。 → つまり、手順4は飛ばすな。
items.speaker: faith
choices: Don't skip step four.
Step four is optional and harmless.
Starting again is quicker.
items.note: technically＝一応。I wouldn't＝やめとけ

items.en: Just fill out the top half and leave the rest to us.
items.ja: 上半分だけ記入して、残りはこちらに任せてください。
items.speaker: rosie
choices: fill out
fill in
feel out
items.note: 書類は米で fill out。fill‿out とつながる
items.tts: Just fill out the top half 'n' leave the rest to us.

items.en: Your new card should arrive in seven to ten business days, but you can start using it in the app today.
items.ja: 新しいカードは7〜10営業日で届きますが、アプリなら今日から使えます。 →「へえ、いいですね。じゃあ、それまではスマホで払えるんですね？」
items.speaker: agnes
choices: Oh, nice. So I can pay with my phone till then?
Sure, I'll show you the card.
No, I only work weekdays.
items.note: business days＝営業日。アプリでは先に使える

items.en: Check-in closes 45 minutes before departure, so with a 7:15 flight, you'll want to be through by 6:30.
items.ja: チェックインは出発45分前に締め切りなので、7時15分の便なら6時半までに済ませてください。
items.speaker: ken
items.note: 7:15の45分前＝6:30。数字三つの役割を分ける
items.tts: Check-in closes forty-five minutes before departure, so with a seven-fifteen flight, you'll wanna be through by six-thirty.
items.ask: 何時までに 手続き？

items.en: I mean, it's your call, but if it were my money, I'd probably sit tight till the new model's out.
items.ja: まあ決めるのは君だけど、僕のお金なら新型が出るまでじっと待つかな。 → つまり、今は買わずに待つのがいい。
items.speaker: lopez
choices: He suggests waiting for the new model.
He thinks you should buy it now.
He's offering to lend you money.
items.note: it's your call の後が本音。sit tight＝じっと待つ

items.en: Honestly, you might as well wait for the sale at this point.
items.ja: 正直、ここまで来たらセールを待ったほうがいいよ。
items.speaker: bunnie
choices: might as well
may as well
might well
items.note: might as well＝〜したほうがまし。as は弱く縮む
items.tts: Honestly, you might's well wait for the sale at this point.

items.en: You might want to double-check that figure before it goes to the client.
items.ja: クライアントに出す前に、その数字をもう一度確認したほうがいいかもね。 → つまり、間違っていると思う。
items.speaker: tia
choices: She thinks the figure is probably wrong.
She has checked it and it's correct.
She wants to send it herself.
items.note: might want to＝やんわりした指示。誤りの示唆
items.tts: You might wanna double-check that figure before it goes to the client.

items.en: You ought to book your tickets early. They tend to sell out by Friday.
items.ja: チケットは早めに取ったほうがいいよ。金曜には売り切れがちだから。
items.speaker: genji
choices: ought to
got to
have to
items.note: oughta＝ought to。gotta（got to）と聞き分け
items.tts: You oughta book your tickets early. They tend to sell out by Friday.

items.en: If you had to pick one, the ryokan in Hakone or the hotel in Yokohama, which would you go for?
items.ja: どちらか一つ選ぶなら、箱根の旅館と横浜のホテル、どっちにする？ →「予算が許すなら箱根。一生に一度だし。」
items.speaker: tammy
choices: Hakone, if the budget stretches. It's a once-in-a-lifetime thing.
I went to Yokohama last spring.
I'll pick you up at the hotel.
items.note: go for＝選ぶ。二択には片方を答える

items.en: It's not that the plan's bad. I just think we're trying to do too much, too soon.
items.ja: 計画が悪いってわけじゃない。ただ、急いで欲張りすぎてる気がするんだ。 → つまり、規模を縮めてゆっくりやるべき。
items.speaker: zucker
choices: They should do less, more slowly.
He thinks the plan is bad.
He wants to move faster.
items.note: It's not that ~. I just…＝本音は後半

items.en: I've escalated this to our technical team. They usually respond within 48 hours.
items.ja: 技術チームに引き継ぎました。通常48時間以内に返答があります。 →「それまでに連絡がなかったら？」
items.speaker: marina
choices: And if I don't hear back by then?
Thanks, I'll take the escalator.
Great, so it's fixed now?
items.note: escalate＝上に回す。まだ解決していない
items.tts: I've escalated this to our technical team. They usually respond within forty-eight hours.

items.en: Unfortunately, that falls outside what I'm able to authorize. But I can put in a request for you.
items.ja: あいにく、それは私の権限を超えています。ですが、代わりに申請を出すことはできます。 → つまり、自分では決められないが上に頼める。
items.speaker: orville
choices: He can't approve it, but he can ask someone who can.
The request is already approved.
He refuses to help at all.
items.note: outside what I can authorize＝権限外。依頼は可

items.en: Your case number is 507713. That's two sevens in the middle.
items.ja: お客様の受付番号は507713です。真ん中は7が二つです。
items.speaker: ken
items.note: two sevens＝77。0は「オー」と読む
items.tts: Your case number is five-oh-seven, seven-one-three. That's two sevens in the middle.

items.en: I'm going to have to put you on hold for a moment while I check with my supervisor. Is that OK?
items.ja: 上の者に確認しますので、少々保留にさせていただいてもよろしいですか？ →「いいですけど、今度は切らないでくださいね。」
items.speaker: lily
choices: That's fine, but please don't cut me off this time.
No, I'm not holding anything.
Sure, my supervisor's out today.
items.note: on hold＝保留。前回切られた不満を添える
items.tts: I'm gonna have to put you on hold for a moment while I check with my supervisor. Is that OK?

items.en: I can't waive the late fee completely, but as a courtesy, I can knock it down to half.
items.ja: 延滞料を全額免除することはできませんが、特別に半額まで下げられます。 → つまり、延滞料は半額になる。
items.speaker: gayle
choices: You pay half the late fee.
You pay no late fee at all.
You pay the full late fee.
items.note: as a courtesy＝特別対応。knock down＝下げる

items.en: Your payment hasn't gone through on our end.
items.ja: こちらでは、お支払いがまだ完了していません。
items.speaker: kid-cat
choices: hasn't
has
had
items.note: hasn't の t はほぼ消える。n の有無で判断
items.tts: Your payment hasn' gone through on our end.

items.en: Before I can do anything, I'll just need you to verify the last four digits of the card.
items.ja: 手続きの前に、カード番号の下4桁で本人確認をお願いします。 →「はい、6018で終わります。」
items.speaker: tangy
choices: Sure, it ends in 6018.
Four? I've only got one card.
Yes, the card is in my name.
items.note: verify＝本人確認。下4桁を言うのが答え

items.en: Take 2 tonight, then 1 every 8 hours, but no more than 6 in 24 hours.
items.ja: 今夜2錠、その後は8時間ごとに1錠。ただし24時間で6錠までです。
items.speaker: pekoe
choices: 6錠
8錠
2錠
items.note: every 8 hours は間隔。上限は no more than の後
items.tts: Take two tonight, then one every eight hours, but no more than six in twenty-four hours.

items.en: It's probably nothing to worry about, but I'd like to rule a few things out, so I'm going to order some blood work.
items.ja: たぶん心配いりませんが、いくつか可能性を除外したいので、血液検査をしましょう。 → つまり、念のため検査する。
items.speaker: nana
choices: It's a blood test, just to be safe.
The doctor has found something serious.
No tests are needed.
items.note: rule out＝可能性を消す。blood work＝血液検査
items.tts: It's probably nothing to worry about, but I'd like to rule a few things out, so I'm gonna order some blood work.

items.en: Call the office and tell them it's been three days, and ask for something stronger.
items.ja: 病院に電話して、もう3日経つって伝えて、もっと強い薬を頼みなよ。
items.speaker: cj
choices: them
him
her
items.note: 'em＝them。him（'im）とは母音で区別
items.tts: Call the office and tell 'em it's been three days, and ask for something stronger.

items.en: You mustn't drive for twenty-four hours after the sedation.
items.ja: 鎮静剤のあと24時間は運転してはいけません。
items.speaker: mabel
choices: mustn't
must
needn't
items.note: mustn't＝禁止。真ん中の t は発音しない
items.tts: You mussn't drive for twenty-four hours after the sedation.

items.en: Good news: it's a sprain rather than a break, so you'll be back on your feet in a couple of weeks.
items.ja: 骨折じゃなくて捻挫だから、2週間くらいで歩けるようになるよ。
items.speaker: dom
choices: sprain
strain
pain
items.note: sprain＝捻挫。strain（筋の損傷）は sp/st で区別

items.en: The doctor's running about forty minutes behind. Are you okay to wait, or would you rather reschedule?
items.ja: 先生は40分ほど遅れています。お待ちになりますか、それとも予約を取り直しますか？ →「待ちます。でもちょっとコーヒーを買いに出てもいいですか？」
items.speaker: bea
choices: I can wait, but could I run out and grab a coffee?
Forty? I booked for four.
No, the doctor ran this morning.
items.note: running behind＝予定より遅れている。走る話ではない

items.en: I'm not saying cut it out altogether. Just maybe not three coffees before lunch.
items.ja: 完全にやめろとは言ってないの。ただ、お昼前に3杯はどうかなって。 → つまり、量を減らして。
items.speaker: marina
choices: Drink less coffee, not none.
Stop drinking coffee completely.
Only drink coffee after lunch.
items.note: cut out＝完全にやめる。言っているのは「減らせ」

items.en: You're free to move out, of course. It's just that the lease requires sixty days' notice, so we'd need that in writing.
items.ja: もちろん退去は自由です。ただ賃貸契約で60日前の通知が必要なので、書面でいただきたいんです。 → つまり、60日前に書面で通知が必要。
items.speaker: henry
choices: You must give sixty days' written notice.
You can move out whenever you like.
The lease ends in sixty days.
items.note: notice＝事前の通知。すぐ出られるわけではない

items.en: Read the fine print, man. There's a twelve-month minimum, and they charge you to leave early.
items.ja: 細かい規約を読みなよ。最低12か月で、途中解約は料金を取られるぞ。 →「本当？途中解約の料金はいくら？」
items.speaker: sterling
choices: Seriously? How much is the early cancellation fee?
I can't read print that small.
Twelve? I've only got eleven.
items.note: fine print＝細則。文字の大きさの話ではない

items.en: Break the lease in the first year and there's a fee of two months' rent, so $3,800.
items.ja: 1年以内に契約を解除すると家賃2か月分の違約金、つまり3,800ドルかかります。
items.speaker: octavian
items.note: thirty-eight hundred＝3,800。bucks＝ドル
items.tts: Break the lease in the first year and there's a fee of two months' rent, so thirty-eight hundred bucks.

items.en: If anything gets broken while we're moving it, we're not liable unless you've bought the extra coverage.
items.ja: 運搬中に何か壊れても、追加の補償に入っていなければ当社は責任を負いません。 → つまり、補償なしなら壊れても弁償なし。
items.speaker: ken
choices: Without extra coverage, they won't pay for damage.
They pay for any damage.
The extra coverage is already included.
items.note: not liable＝責任を負わない。coverage＝補償

items.en: You'll get your deposit back, minus any deductions for damage.
items.ja: 敷金は返ってくるよ。傷みの分を差し引いてね。
items.speaker: tom-nook
choices: deductions
reductions
deduction
items.note: deductions＝差し引き。reductions と頭の音で区別

items.en: We'd need you to sign today to lock in this rate.
items.ja: この料金を確保するには、本日ご署名いただく必要があります。 →「先に契約書を持ち帰って読みたいです。」
items.speaker: fang
choices: I'd rather take the contract home and read it first.
Sure, I'll lock the door on my way out.
No, I signed up yesterday.
items.note: 即日署名の圧力。持ち帰るのが賢い返し

items.en: The Airbnb was $1,140 for three nights, plus a $60 cleaning fee, split four ways.
items.ja: Airbnbは3泊で1,140ドル、プラス清掃費60ドル。それを4人で割り勘ね。
items.speaker: audie
items.tts: The Airbnb was eleven-forty for three nights, plus a sixty-dollar cleaning fee, split four ways.

items.en: On paper it's ¥380,000, but after tax and insurance I take home about ¥290,000.
items.ja: 額面は38万円だけど、税金と保険を引くと手取りは29万円くらいなんだ。
items.speaker: pietro
choices: 29万円
38万円
9万円
items.note: on paper＝額面。take home＝手取り
items.tts: On paper it's three hundred and eighty thousand, but after tax and insurance I take home about two hundred and ninety thousand.

items.en: The electric bill's ¥11,800 this month, almost double last month's ¥6,200. It's the heater.
items.ja: 今月の電気代は1万1,800円で、先月の6,200円のほぼ倍。暖房のせいだね。
items.speaker: molly
items.note: almost double は概算。実額は最初の数字
items.tts: The electric bill's eleven thousand eight hundred this month, almost double last month's six thousand two hundred. It's the heater.

items.en: Oh, come on, I would've split it with you if you'd just asked.
items.ja: もう、言ってくれれば割り勘にしたのに。
items.speaker: rosie
choices: would've
could've
should've
items.note: woulda＝would have。could／should は頭の音で区別
items.tts: Oh, come on, I woulda split it with ya if you'd just asked.

items.en: You got the last round, so this one's on me. And no, I'm not taking no for an answer.
items.ja: この前は君がおごったから、今回は僕が払う。断ってもだめだよ。 → つまり、絶対に自分が払う。
items.speaker: stitches
choices: He insists on paying this time.
He wants you to pay again.
He's turning down a drink.
items.note: this one's on me＝おごる。断らせない

items.en: The base is $92K, with up to 15% bonus, so in a good year, just over $105K.
items.ja: 基本給は9万2千ドル、ボーナスは最大15％。いい年なら10万5千ドルを少し超えるわ。
items.speaker: judy
items.note: base＝基本給。105Kはボーナス込みの額
items.tts: The base is ninety-two K, with up to fifteen percent bonus, so in a good year, just over a hundred and five.

items.en: Just so you know, the quote didn't include tax or delivery.
items.ja: 念のためですが、見積もりには税金と配送料が含まれていませんでした。
items.speaker: gulliver
choices: didn't
did
doesn't
items.note: didn't の t は弱い。過去の否定を聞き逃さない
items.tts: Just so you know, the quote didn' include tax or delivery.

items.en: Remote work's great in theory. In practice, I end up answering emails at eleven at night.
items.ja: リモートワークは理屈では最高。でも実際は、夜11時にメールに返信する羽目になる。 → つまり、仕事と私生活の境がなくなる。
items.speaker: beau
choices: Working from home blurs work and free time.
He loves working late at night.
He prefers the office in every way.
items.note: in theory／in practice の対比。後半が本音

items.en: Kyoto's beautiful, but honestly, I can't face the crowds at Fushimi Inari again.
items.ja: 京都はすてきだけど、正直、伏見稲荷の人混みはもう勘弁。 →「夜明けに行きなよ。7時前ならほぼ誰もいないよ。」
items.speaker: katt
choices: Go at dawn. It's practically empty before seven.
Face the crowds? Sure, take a photo.
I've never been to Fushimi Inari either.
items.note: can't face＝気が重くて無理。顔の話ではない

items.en: AI's great for a first draft. I just wouldn't let it anywhere near the final version.
items.ja: AIは下書きには最高。ただ、最終版には絶対に触らせないね。 → つまり、AIは下書き用だけ。
items.speaker: goldie
choices: She only trusts AI for first drafts.
She trusts AI with the final version.
She doesn't use AI at all.
items.note: wouldn't let it anywhere near＝絶対に任せない

items.en: Would you rather have a bigger place out in Saitama, or something tiny in central Tokyo?
items.ja: 埼玉の広めの家と、都心の狭い家、どっちがいい？ →「狭くても都心。長い通勤はいやだな。」
items.speaker: bob
choices: Tiny and central. I'd hate a long commute.
I'd rather have a bigger salary.
Yes, I would.
items.note: 二択の質問に Yes／No で答える罠

items.en: Cold plunges? Hey, if it works for you, more power to you. I'll stick to a hot bath.
items.ja: 冷水浴？まあ、君に合うならどうぞご自由に。僕は熱い風呂で十分。 → つまり、自分はやる気がない。
items.speaker: teddy
choices: He's not interested in trying it.
He's going to try one soon.
He thinks cold plunges are dangerous.
items.note: more power to you＝どうぞご自由に。自分はやらない

items.en: Apparently something like 36 million tourists came last year, and half of them were in my neighborhood konbini.
items.ja: 去年は観光客が3,600万人くらい来たらしいよ。で、その半分がうちの近所のコンビニにいた。
items.speaker: frett
items.note: half はジョーク。数字は thirty-six million
items.tts: Apparently somethin' like thirty-six million tourists came last year, and half of them were in my neighborhood konbini.

items.en: While you're at it, could you also add a booking page? Should be quick, right? Happy to, but that's outside the original scope, so it'd be a separate quote. Ah. Roughly what are we talking? Ballpark, another three or four days' work. I'll send something over tonight.
items.ja: 追加料金がかかり、見積もりが送られてくる。
items.speaker: judy
choices: It'll cost extra, and he'll send a quote.
He'll add it for free because it's quick.
He'll finish the page tonight.
items.ask: 追加の 仕事は どうなる？
items.note: scope＝契約範囲。tonight は見積もりの送付

lines.en: While you're at it, could you also add a booking page? Should be quick, right?

items.ja: 1営業日以内にご連絡がいくはずです。
items.speaker: tia
choices: You should hear back within one business day.
About forty minutes, like before.
I can escalate it to a supervisor.
items.ask: つぎの ひとことは？
items.note: realistically＝本当のところ。期間で答える

lines.ja: お怒りはごもっともです。私にできるのは、本日中に上の者へ上げることです。

lines.en: And how long will that take, realistically?
lines.ja: で、実際のところ、どのくらいかかるんですか？

items.en: Sorry to cut in, but we've got five minutes left and we haven't touched the budget. Fair point. Can we give it ten minutes at the start of Thursday's call? Works for me, as long as finance can join.
items.ja: 木曜の電話会議の冒頭に回る。
items.speaker: goldie
choices: It moves to the start of Thursday's call.
They'll finish it in the next five minutes.
Finance will decide it alone.
items.ask: 予算の話は どうなる？
items.note: five minutes は残り時間。予算は木曜へ

lines.ja: 割り込んでごめん、でも残り5分で予算にまったく触れてないよ。

lines.ja: もっともだ。木曜の電話会議の最初の10分を充てようか？

lines.en: Works for me, as long as finance can join.
lines.ja: それでいいよ、経理も入れるならね。

items.en: So, good news and bad news. The good news is the leak's fixed. And the bad news? The floor underneath is rotten, so we're looking at another week and about two grand.
items.ja: 2千ドル？ まず書面でもらえますか？
items.speaker: zucker
choices: Two grand? Can I get that in writing first?
Great, so you're all done?
Another week? Sure, I'll grab a coffee.
items.ask: つぎの ひとことは？
items.note: grand＝千ドル。直ったで終わりではない

lines.en: So, good news and bad news. The good news is the leak's fixed.
lines.ja: さて、いい知らせと悪い知らせがある。いい知らせは、水漏れは直った。

lines.en: And the bad news?
lines.ja: で、悪い知らせは？

lines.en: The floor underneath is rotten, so we're looking at another week and about two grand.
lines.ja: 下の床が腐ってて、あと1週間と2千ドルくらいかかりそうだ。
lines.tts: The floor underneath is rotten, so we're lookin' at another week and about two grand.

items.en: Your blood pressure's a little on the high side. Not dangerous, but I'd like to keep an eye on it. So do I need to start taking something? Not yet. Cut back on salt, walk a little more, and we'll recheck in three months.
items.ja: 薬はまだ不要。減塩と運動のあと再検査。
items.speaker: reneigh
choices: No medicine yet: less salt, more walking, then a recheck.
He has to start medicine today.
His blood pressure is dangerous.
items.note: Not yet＝まだ不要。3か月後に再検査

lines.en: Your blood pressure's a little on the high side. Not dangerous, but I'd like to keep an eye on it.
lines.ja: 血圧が少し高めですね。危険ではありませんが、様子を見ておきたいです。

lines.en: So do I need to start taking something?
lines.ja: じゃあ、何か薬を飲み始めないといけませんか？

lines.en: Not yet. Cut back on salt, walk a little more, and we'll recheck in three months.
lines.ja: まだです。塩分を控えて、もう少し歩いて、3か月後に再検査しましょう。

items.en: Okay, the total's $312, and Jess only had a salad. So do we split it evenly or figure out who had what? Evenly's easier, but it feels kind of rough on Jess.
items.ja: 彼女のサラダ代を引いて、残りを割ろう。
items.speaker: poppy
choices: Let's take her salad off and split the rest.
Sure, I'll have a salad too.
Rough? The steak was fine.
items.ask: つぎの ひとことは？
items.note: rough on〜＝〜に不公平。料理の話ではない

lines.en: Okay, the total's $312, and Jess only had a salad.
lines.ja: えっと、合計312ドルで、ジェスはサラダだけだったよね。
lines.tts: Okay, the total's three-twelve, and Jess only had a salad.

lines.en: So do we split it evenly or figure out who had what?
lines.ja: じゃあ均等に割る？ それとも誰が何を食べたか計算する？

lines.en: Evenly's easier, but it feels kind of rough on Jess.
lines.ja: 均等が楽だけど、ジェスにはちょっと不公平な気がする。

items.en: So when do I get my deposit back? Within thirty days, minus cleaning. And the wall where the shelf was, that'll need patching. The shelf was there when I moved in, though. It's in the move-in photos.
items.ja: 壁の補修費は払う必要がない。
items.speaker: bunnie
choices: She shouldn't have to pay for the wall.
She wants the shelf back.
She'll pay for the cleaning and the wall.
items.ask: 女性が 言いたいことは？
items.note: 入居時からある＝修理費は払わない主張

lines.en: So when do I get my deposit back?
lines.ja: で、敷金はいつ返ってきますか？

lines.en: The shelf was there when I moved in, though. It's in the move-in photos.
lines.ja: でも、あの棚は入居時からありましたよ。入居時の写真に写ってます。

items.en: Honestly, half our team could be replaced by AI in five years. Replaced? Or just doing different work? Potato, potahto. Either way, nobody's job looks the same.
items.ja: かもね、でも「違う」と「なくなる」は別だよ。
items.speaker: wolfgang
choices: Maybe, but 'different' isn't the same as 'gone'.
I like potatoes either way.
Five years? I've been here six.
items.ask: つぎの ひとことは？
items.note: Potato, potahto＝言い方の違いだけ

lines.en: Honestly, half our team could be replaced by AI in five years.
lines.ja: 正直、5年でうちのチームの半分はAIに置き換わるかもね。

lines.en: Replaced? Or just doing different work?
lines.ja: 置き換わる？ それとも違う仕事をするだけ？

lines.en: Potato, potahto. Either way, nobody's job looks the same.
lines.ja: 言い方の違いだよ。どっちにしろ、誰の仕事も今のままじゃない。

items.en: There's a ¥23,000 roaming charge on my bill, and I had data roaming turned off. I see it. It looks like your phone connected to a ship network on the ferry. A ship network? Nobody mentioned that. It happens a lot. I can waive it this time, as a one-time thing.
items.ja: 今回に限り免除される。
items.speaker: francine
choices: It's canceled, just this once.
She has to pay ¥23,000.
It's split in half.
items.note: waive＝免除。one-time thing＝今回だけ

lines.ja: 請求書に2万3千円のローミング料金がありますけど、データローミングは切ってたんです。
lines.tts: There's a twenty-three thousand yen roaming charge on my bill, and I had data roaming turned off.

lines.en: It happens a lot. I can waive it this time, as a one-time thing.
lines.ja: よくあることです。今回に限り免除いたします。

items.en: We were going to do Kyoto in April, but everyone says it's wall-to-wall tourists. It is. Have you thought about Kanazawa? Similar feel, a fraction of the crowds. Ooh. And the bullet train goes straight there now, doesn't it?
items.ja: そう。東京から2時間半くらいだよ。
items.speaker: whitney

Yes, it's wall-to-wall in April.
No, the bullet train only goes to Kyoto in April.
items.ask: つぎの ひとことは？
items.note: 付加疑問は確認。所要時間で答えるのが自然

lines.en: We were going to do Kyoto in April, but everyone says it's wall-to-wall tourists.

lines.tts: We were gonna do Kyoto in April, but everyone says it's wall-to-wall tourists.

lines.en: Ooh. And the bullet train goes straight there now, doesn't it?
lines.ja: へえ。今は新幹線で直通なんだよね？

items.ja: もっともだ。15日にもう一度話そう。
items.speaker: label

Tight? I'll loosen the budget, then.
Yes, you took on the new hires.
items.ask: つぎの ひとことは？
items.note: put a date on it＝日付を決めて。日で答える

lines.en: I've taken on the Chicago account and the new hires. I'd like to talk about my salary.
lines.ja: シカゴの担当と新人教育を引き受けました。給与について話したいです。

lines.en: I appreciate that. Could we put a date on it?
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。日付を決めてもらえますか？

items.en: I'm here to renew my residence card. Is it just this form? That one, your passport, a photo, and proof of employment. Did you book online? Book? I didn't realize you had to. You don't, strictly, but walk-ins can wait two hours or more.
items.ja: 手続きはできるが、長く待つかもしれない。
items.speaker: kid-cat

He has to book online and come back.
He only needs the form.
items.ask: 男性について わかることは？

items.ja: わかってる。それが引っかかってるの。

OK, then I'll tell you what to do.

lines.ja: シンガポールの仕事、受けるべきかな？ 給料がずっといいの。

lines.en: I mean, I'd never tell you what to do. But you did say you wanted to be near your folks.
lines.ja: まあ、どうしろとは絶対言わないけど。でも、家族の近くにいたいって言ってたよね。

items.en: Why's the gym still charging me? I stopped going in March. Did you actually cancel, though? Those contracts auto-renew unless you give thirty days' notice. Hang on, so not going isn't cancelling?
items.ja: 解約していないので、まだ払っている。
items.speaker: cyd
choices: He never cancelled, so he's still paying.
The gym charged him by mistake.
He cancelled in March with notice.
items.note: 行かない≠解約。30日前の通知が要る

lines.en: Why's the gym still charging me? I stopped going in March.
lines.ja: なんでジムからまだ請求が来るんだ？ 3月から行ってないのに。

lines.en: Did you actually cancel, though? Those contracts auto-renew unless you give thirty days' notice.
lines.ja: でも、ちゃんと解約した？ ああいう契約は30日前に通知しないと自動更新だよ。

lines.en: Hang on, so not going isn't cancelling?
lines.ja: ちょっと待って、行かないだけじゃ解約にならないのか？

items.en: Can I take these with the antibiotics I'm on? Should be fine, but leave a couple of hours between them, and steer clear of alcohol till the course is done. Not even one beer on the weekend?
items.ja: ごめんなさい、全部飲み終わるまではだめです。
items.speaker: kicks
choices: Sorry, not until you've finished the whole course.
Of course, a couple of hours is fine.
On the weekend? We're open Saturdays.
items.ask: つぎの ひとことは？
items.note: steer clear of＝避ける。course＝服用期間

lines.en: Can I take these with the antibiotics I'm on?
lines.ja: 今飲んでいる抗生物質と一緒に、これを飲んでもいいですか？

lines.en: Should be fine, but leave a couple of hours between them, and steer clear of alcohol till the course is done.
lines.ja: 大丈夫だと思いますが、2時間ほど間を空けて、飲み終わるまでお酒は控えてください。

lines.en: Not even one beer on the weekend?
lines.ja: 週末にビール1杯もだめですか？

items.en: Evening. Sorry to bother you, but your trash cans have been out on the curb since Tuesday. Oh, have they? Pickup's Thursday, isn't it? It moved to Monday last month. There was a notice.

lines.ja: あら、そうでした？ 収集は木曜ですよね？

items.en: Quick update. I'm done with the login page, just waiting on design for the icons. Same boat, sort of. I can't test payments till the API keys come through. Who's following up on the keys? Because that's blocking both of us now.

lines.ja: キーは誰が催促してる？ もう二人とも止まってるよ。

items.en: Do I need to file a tax return if my company already does the year-end adjustment? Not usually, unless you had side income over two hundred thousand yen. Ah. My weekend coaching made about three hundred thousand.
items.ja: じゃあ、たぶん申告が必要だね。
items.speaker: hamlet
choices: Then you'll probably need to file one.
Great, your company will handle it.
Three hundred? That's under the limit, then.
items.ask: つぎの ひとことは？
items.note: 副業30万＞20万。申告が必要

lines.ja: あ。週末のコーチで30万くらい稼いだんだ。

items.en: Have you heard? They want us in the office four days a week from January. Four? I moved to Kamakura because they said remote was permanent. I know. Apparently 'permanent' meant 'until further notice'.
items.ja: 二人とも変更に不満がある。

They're glad to go back to the office.
They think it's only two days a week.
